page: Amazon Web Services c9g.medium is a compute-optimized instance powered by a custom AWS Graviton Gen9 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 microarchitecture running at 3.3 GHz. The processor is equipped with 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It includes hardware-accelerated AES cryptography but lacks AVX, AMX, and hyper-threading capabilities. The instance is provisioned with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded execution in specific workloads. The c9g.medium achieves top-tier performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 16.83 GB/sec and strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.12 GB/sec. However, due to its single-core configuration, multi-core stress-ng benchmarks and Passmark CPU scores are rated as poor. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 38.46 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 13.36 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance are relatively weak, executing 3.3 million operations per second. For lightweight machine learning, it processes text generation on a small 135M LLM model at an average speed of 84.44 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c9g.medium offers a low-entry point to the Graviton9 ARM ecosystem, providing dedicated compute resources without the overhead of multi-core licensing or unused memory capacity. The primary tradeoff is the strict single-vCPU limitation and low memory ceiling, which restricts its utility for parallel processing or memory-intensive databases. This instance is best suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, simple utility scripting, and microservices that benefit from ARMv9 architectural efficiencies without requiring high memory density.

Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this arm64 instance features 1 dedicated vCPU, 2.0 GB of system memory, and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, with no local storage or GPU acceleration. Performance benchmarks show exceptional single-threaded capabilities, particularly in bzip3 decompression and gzip compression, though multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics remain low due to the single-core architecture.
